activity.notes: Hattusili I was an early Hittite Great King whose campaigns in northern Syria belong to the formative Old Kingdom. Absolute Hittite chronology remains reconstructed rather than directly fixed by regnal-year evidence, so ATLAS stores the conventional c. 1650-c. 1620 BCE interval with approximate boundaries and reuses the existing Hittite Kingdom polity and Great King role used for Old Kingdom rulers.

sources.title: New evidence for Middle Bronze Age chronology from the Syro-Anatolian frontier
sources.citation_text: The peer-reviewed Antiquity study links the destruction chronology of Zincirli to campaigns probably undertaken in the reign of Hattusili I and states that the radiocarbon evidence affirms the traditional estimate for his reign while emphasizing reconstructed absolute chronology.
